what_its_for: Sinecatechins is a cream used to treat genital and anal warts (called condylomata acuminata) in adults with healthy immune systems. It is made from a green tea leaf extract. It does NOT cure the virus that causes warts, but it helps clear the visible warts.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after applying this cream. Apply a thin layer of the cream directly to each wart using your finger. Do NOT put it inside the vagina, anus, urethra (urine opening), or mouth. Do NOT cover the treated area with a bandage or wrap. You may wear loose-fitting clothing over the area. Do NOT wash off the cream between doses — simply apply the next dose at the scheduled time.
dosing: Apply the cream 3 times a day (for example, morning, afternoon, and evening) to all of your warts. Continue using it for up to 16 weeks, or until all warts are completely gone, whichever comes first. Use only a small pea-sized amount (about 0.5 cm strand) per wart. Do not use more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply the cream as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next regular application, skip the missed one and go back to your normal schedule. Do NOT double up or apply extra to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the tube in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F or 2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze. You may also keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 7 days when needed for convenience. Keep the cap tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT have sexual contact (vaginal, anal, or oral) while the cream is on your skin, as it may cause irritation to your partner. Use a condom if you are sexually active, as sinecatechins can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms — talk to your doctor about alternative contraception. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Avoid sun exposure on the treated area. Do NOT use other creams, lotions, or skin products on the treated area unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience: severe skin reactions such as intense burning, pain, swelling, blistering, open sores, or bleeding at the application site; signs of infection in the treated area (increasing redness, warmth, pus, or fever); the warts spread or get significantly worse; you develop a rash or allergic reaction anywhere on your body; or you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Most people start to see improvement in their warts within a few weeks, but full clearance may take up to 16 weeks of regular use. It is very important to keep using the cream even if you do not see immediate results. Some skin irritation and redness at the treated area is common and usually means the medicine is working.
special_populations: This medication is NOT approved for use in children or teenagers under 18 years old. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this cream, as its safety has not been fully established in these situations. People with weakened immune systems (such as those with HIV or on immunosuppressive medicines) should talk to their doctor, as this medication was studied in people with healthy immune systems.
